did_you_know.text: Did you know? After Nahash, king of the Ammonites, died, his son Hanun ascended to the throne.
Did you know? David sent his servants to comfort Hanun because, as he said, Nahash had shown him kindness. The delegation was therefore sent as a gesture of goodwill, not as an act of war.
Did you know? Hanun humiliated David’s messengers in two ways: he shaved off half their beards and cut their garments in half, up to their buttocks.
Did you know? David did not immediately bring the messengers back to Jerusalem. Instead, because they were deeply ashamed, he told them to remain in Jericho until their beards grew back.
Did you know? When the Ammonites realized that they had made themselves enemies of David, they hired armies from Aram-naharaim, Aram-maacah, and Zobah, paying a thousand talents of silver for them.

Did you know? The Aramean forces they hired included thirty-two thousand chariots, as well as the king of Maacah and his people. They camped near Medeba, while the Ammonites gathered from their cities.
Did you know? Joab had to fight on two fronts: the Arameans were in front of him, and the Ammonites were behind him. So he divided the army between himself and his brother Abishai.

Did you know? Before the battle, Joab encouraged Abishai with the words, “Be strong, and let us be courageous,” for the sake of the people and the cities of their God, and he entrusted the outcome to the Lord.

Did you know? After their first defeat, the Arameans recruited additional forces from across the Euphrates. In response, David gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and personally led the campaign.
Did you know? Following the defeat of the Arameans, the servants of Hadadezer made peace with David and served him, and Aram ceased helping the Ammonites.
